title: Mirabel and the Alibi
premise: Yara Okafor, the unassuming archivist of St. Verena's Cathedral, has spent years quietly untangling deaths the police mislabeled as accidents, keeping his gift hidden behind locked crypt doors. When a drowned man is found wearing clothes stolen from Yara's own closet, the police finally see him — not as an ally, but as their prime suspect. To clear his name, Yara must reopen the one case the city buried: the death of Judge Anselm Reyes, ruled accidental seven years ago, whose trial-adjacent secrets could topple half the cathedral's benefactors. As the anniversary trial of a related case approaches, Yara races to prove the judge was murdered by someone still inside the cathedral's inner circle, ending with Yara exposing the killer in open court and choosing to surrender his anonymity rather than let an innocent man hang for his alibi.
about_author: Petra Nakamura is a former parish records clerk who spent a decade cataloguing centuries of births, marriages, and quiet scandals before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about people who know too much because they were never supposed to be noticed.

chapters.title: The Locked Crypt
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. We meet him cataloguing the cathedral crypt, where he keeps private files on three 'accidents' he quietly solved. The beat is controlled solitude — a man who has made invisibility an art form, comfortable in the margins.

chapters.title: A Body in Borrowed Clothes
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A drowned man washes up at the canal dock wearing Yara's own missing coat and scarf. Police find the clothes traced to his closet; suddenly the invisible man is visible, suspected. Beat: fear cracking open routine.

chapters.title: Detective Ilse Brandt
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. A sharp, skeptical detective interviews Yara, who must decide how much of his past casework to reveal. He offers nothing, which makes her more curious. Beat: cat-and-mouse tension, mutual recognition of intelligence.

chapters.title: What the Closet Knew
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. He reconstructs when the clothes were taken — during the cathedral's restoration gala, meaning the thief had access to staff areas. Beat: dread mixed with the old thrill of deduction returning.

chapters.title: The Case Everyone Swore Was Closed
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. He pulls his oldest file: Judge Anselm Reyes, dead seven years ago, ruled a fall. The drowned man turns out to be a former court clerk from that case. Beat: the two cases fuse; stakes escalate.

chapters.title: Sister Agnes Remembers
chapters.summary: Agnes's POV. An elderly nun recalls the night Reyes died — lights on in the bell tower, a second voice. She's frightened and asks Yara to stop digging. Beat: guilt and warning; the past pushing back.

chapters.title: Trial Date Set
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. The prosecution sets a trial date for Yara in six weeks, tied politically to the anniversary proceedings around the Reyes estate. Brandt doubts the evidence but follows orders. Beat: clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: The Benefactors' Circle
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. He maps who profited from Reyes's death — a restoration fund, a land easement, a bishop's appointment. All roads lead inside the cathedral. Beat: betrayal of the institution he loves.

chapters.title: Someone in the Stacks
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. His archive office is searched; his private case files are gone. Only three people knew where they were kept. Beat: violation and paranoia — his sanctuary is no longer safe.

chapters.title: An Alibi Made of Silence
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. Brandt finds Yara's timeline for the drowning night has a two-hour hole — the same hours Reyes died seven years ago. Coincidence or frame? Beat: suspicion deepening on both sides.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. He tracks the gala's guest list and finds a name forged in the ledger — someone signed in who never attended. Beat: first hard evidence of premeditation, and hope.

chapters.title: Midnight in the Bell Tower
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Following Agnes's memory, he examines the tower and finds a repaired railing and fresh mortar dated to the week after Reyes fell. Beat: confirmation the fall was staged — and that he's being watched.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Price
chapters.summary: Father Emmerich's POV. The cathedral's dean knows more than he says and warns Yara that exposing Reyes's murder will destroy the parish that sheltered him. Beat: loyalty versus truth made explicit and personal.

chapters.title: The Second Body
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. Sister Agnes is found dead — another 'accident,' another staged scene. Brandt privately concludes Yara can't be the killer but publicly the case against him strengthens. Beat: grief and urgency.

chapters.title: Reading the Ashes
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Agnes left him a coded note in the hymnal they both loved, naming a date and a phrase from the Reyes verdict. Beat: the dead woman speaking; resolve hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Man Who Signed In
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. He identifies the forged gala guest: the cathedral's conservator, Tomas Vey, who restored the tower railings and handled Reyes's estate papers. Beat: the shape of the killer emerging.

chapters.title: Frame Job
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. Someone plants Yara's fingerprints on Agnes's window latch. Brandt hides the evidence from her own captain, crossing a line. Beat: the detective becomes complicit in justice outside the law.

chapters.title: What Vey Buried
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. In the crypt records he finds Vey altered Reyes's will — the judge had discovered embezzlement in the restoration fund days before dying. Beat: motive fully revealed; the conspiracy has roots everywhere.

chapters.title: The Trap in the Crypt
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara lets word slip that the original will survives, then waits among the tombs. Vey comes for it at night; Yara confronts him and barely escapes alive when Vey realizes the trap. Beat: terror, near-death, commitment.

chapters.title: Confession Interrupted
chapters.summary: Vey's POV. Cornered and believing himself doomed, Vey confesses to Father Emmerich — who, bound by the seal, can only act if Vey waives it. Vey, arrogant, assumes no one will ever hear. Beat: dramatic irony at its sharpest.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Trial
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. At the reopened Reyes inquest, Yara takes the stand as a suspect and turns testimony into revelation: the will, the mortar, the forged signature, and Vey's waived confession delivered by Emmerich. Beat: climax — truth spoken aloud at last.

chapters.title: Belonging
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, coda. Charges dropped, Yara chooses to stay at the cathedral — not invisible now, but known. Brandt leaves her card on his desk: an invitation, not a summons. Beat: resolution — belonging found not in hiding, but in being seen.
